messages:
alex: Heads-up: onboarding CI flaked on SDK vs REST parity. REST POST /routes/rollout returns 202 but node SDK retries on 409 and ends up triggering duplicate rollouts.
ravi: Which SDK version?
alex: node v1.16.3 in our sample-app. repro: REST:
```bash
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"route_id":"r1","version":"v2"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/routes/rollout
```
SDK:
```js
const c = new RedwoodClient({token:process.env.T});
await c.routes.rollout({route_id:'r1', version:'v2'}); // retried after 409 -> duplicate effect
```
taylor: 409 here is a concurrent-mod signal. Server expects caller to either backoff and refresh or use an idempotency key. SDK retrying blindly is wrong for mutating endpoints.
alex: Agreed. Also noticed our sample-cli doesn't attach idempotency keys by default. That makes POST non-idempotent under retries.
ravi: We changed the SDK retry set last quarter; looks like the node SDK treats 409 as retryable. We should align with the canonical retry table: only retry idempotent HTTP methods (GET, HEAD, PUT with idempotency) and server 503/504/429 with Retry-After. 409 shouldn't be auto-retried for rollouts.
taylor: Quick action items: (1) patch node SDK to not retry 409 on POST /routes/rollout, (2) sample-cli: add optional idempotency-key header for mutating calls and enable by default for sample-app, (3) add e2e test covering rollout double-apply.
ci-bot: Filed issue: devex/1074 "sdk-retry-409-rollout-duplication" and attached failing CI log.
alex: For teams hit now, workaround: call REST directly from CI or set idempotency-key manually. I'll add a note in sample-app README.
ravi: I'll draft the SDK change and ping @taylor for review.
taylor: I'll add test case and update retry docs. Let's also add a small linter in SDK to warn when retrying non-idempotent endpoints without idempotency-key. :warning:
alex: Thanks — saved our onboarding run.
